title: Rey and the Magic Branch
markdown:
The sun felt warm on Rey’s face, the same warmth as before he discovered the juiciest apples you ever did see. A big warm wink of a day. The air smelled like a sweet sugary dream. Nana Tess’s apples were the juiciest, sunniest apples in the whole wide world. But a grumpy grey frown of a problem stood in the way: the orchard gate, shut tight, jammed like a stubborn pebble.

“Hmph!” Rey pushed with his little hands until his cheeks went pink and his sneakers squeaked. The gate didn’t budge. Not even a wiggle.

Saffron the parrot, feathers a rainbow of sunshine and berries, bobbed on his shoulder. “Stuck! Stuck! Grumpy gate!” She pecked the metal. Clang.

Nana Tess arrived, basket swinging like a happy pendulum. “Oh my. This old gate has a mind of its own today.” A firm push. A strong pull. Still stuck. Rey’s shoulders drooped like wilting flowers. Tummy flip-flop. He wanted apple-y goodness right now.

“It’s no use,” he sighed, a little wobbly. “We’ll never get our apple adventure.”

Nana Tess spotted a flurry of fallen leaves skittering near the gate. “Aha!” Her long bristly broom: bristly end on the ground, press the handle. The leaves flew.

“Look, Rey! See how this end goes down, and that end goes up?”

Rey squinted. A wobbly dance. Broom down, leaves up. He scampered to the garden edge, where a long fallen branch waited. A small smooth stone. He wedged the branch under the stone and pushed the other end. The stone lifted, a tiny tiny bit.

“Whoa!” Saffron ruffled. “Wow! Wow! Clever Rey!”

Another branch, much much longer. Same stone, same wedge. Push. Pop! The stone jumped higher. And it felt much much easier.

“It’s easier with the long one!” Surprise fizzed instead of frustration. “The longer the branch, the less I have to push!” A super-duper puzzle.

“Nana Tess! I know how to open the gate!” The longest strongest branch. Saffron’s speedy song: “Lift! Lift! Smarty-pants Rey!” Nana Tess helping heave. One end tucked under the heavy stuck gate, close to the jam. The other end stuck out, long and ready.

“Okay.” A big brave breath. “Here we go!” He pushed down with all his might on the far end. Creak! The gate lifted. Just a little, but it lifted.

“It’s working!” Saffron flapped like a tiny aeroplane. Rey pushed again, a little harder. A gap just big enough.

“Hooray!” Nana Tess’s smile as wide as the orchard. “We did it, explorers!”

They wriggled through. Sweet sun-warmed apple scent, a happy hug. Rey’s tummy, no longer flipping, felt full and proud.

Back among the trees, munching a big juicy apple that dripped down his chin, he looked at the sturdy branch. “That branch. It was like a magic helper for lifting!”

Nana Tess wiped juice from his cheek. “It is, in a way. That’s called a lever, Rey. When you push down on one end of a strong bar, it helps you lift something very heavy on the other end. Hard work, much much easier.”

Rey’s eyes popped. “A lever! So that’s why the long branch worked better!”

He did not ask what other secrets hid in plain sight. He took another happy bite, and Saffron stole a pip, and the gate, left a little open, remembered how to move if you gave it a long enough branch and a push at the far end.
